Run the Impeccable audit and critique over the map, nodes, chat panel in all three modes, sidebar, menus, branch form, suggestions, diagram and video cards, and empty, loading, error and signed-out states. Fix the findings that affect comprehension, consistency or accessibility; list the rest with reasons.
2. Accessibility: keyboard reachability and visible focus everywhere, sensible focus return, names and roles for every control, live-region announcements that are neither missing nor noisy, contrast in both colour schemes, reduced-motion behaviour for every transition, and 200% zoom.
3. Responsive: narrow windows, very wide windows and the chat-fills-workspace breakpoint.
4. Consistency: spacing, type scale, icon use, wording of labels and errors; Astryx components and tokens only, no raw colours or pixel values.
5. Performance sanity: bundle size after Mermaid and other additions, lazy loading where it helps, and no layout shift when chat opens.
6. Record before and after evidence and the remaining known issues under docs/verification.

## Start here

DESIGN.md, PRODUCT.md, the Impeccable and Astryx skills, src/ChatPage.tsx, src/TreeOverview.tsx and the stylesheet.

## Out of scope

New features, a redesign of the agreed map-first layout, and a theme picker.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- The audit's blocking and major findings are fixed; remaining findings are listed with a reason each.
- The full keyboard journey passes with visible focus and correct focus return, including media and suggestion controls.
- Contrast passes in both colour schemes; every transition respects reduced motion; the app is usable at 200% zoom and in a narrow window.

title: Package first run: one start command, preflight checks and a user guide
description:
## What to build

Make TreeTutor something a learner can start and trust on their own machine without reading the source: one command, clear preflight messages, safe upgrades of saved data and a user guide.

## Work order

1. Start: a single documented command builds when the built assets are missing or stale, starts the loopback server and prints the address. A busy port gives a clear message and an option to choose another. Binding stays loopback-only.
2. Preflight: on start, report the Node version requirement, whether the Claude Code CLI is installed and signed in, and whether Codex is connected, each with the exact next step. A missing provider never blocks opening saved trees.
3. Saved data: record a schema version, and copy the database to a dated backup before any migration that rewrites data. A database from each earlier commit's schema still opens. Print the data directory location, and document backup and restore.
4. Shutdown: stopping the server ends active replies cleanly and marks them interrupted, as the store already does on start.

title: Rename and delete chats and branches
description:
## What to build

Let the learner rename any conversation, delete a whole chat, and delete a branch together with its descendants.

## Work order

1. Rename: an inline rename for the chat header title and the sidebar entry, saved through a new endpoint with the existing 200-character bound. A renamed root is never retitled by a later first question.
2. Delete a chat: removes the root, every descendant, their messages, branches, artifacts and layout in one transaction, after a confirmation that names the chat and its number of conversations. Deleting the open chat moves to the next saved chat or the New chat state.
3. Delete a branch: removes that conversation and its descendants only; the parent conversation and its messages are untouched. Selection moves to the parent.
4. Stop any active reply in a conversation being deleted and ignore its late events. Remove artifact files that belong to deleted conversations.
5. Confirmation is keyboard accessible, focuses the safe choice first and returns focus sensibly afterwards. There is no undo, so the confirmation says so.
6. Integration tests for cascade, transaction rollback on failure, active-reply handling, ownership and CSRF.

title: Render Markdown, code and math in replies with exact passage anchors
description:
## What to build

Show tutor replies as formatted text: headings, lists, emphasis, tables, code blocks with highlighting and math. Passage selection, branch anchors and source reveal must stay exact against the saved raw message text, which remains the canonical source.

## Work order

1. Renderer: choose a Markdown renderer that exposes source positions and add it with the smallest dependency set; record the choice. Raw HTML in replies is not rendered. Links open safely in a new tab and never navigate the app. The Content-Security-Policy stays free of unsafe script sources.
2. Offsets: every rendered text node carries the start offset of its source text. Map a DOM selection back to raw UTF-16 start and end offsets through those markers, so the anchor's text is still an exact slice of the saved message and the branches endpoint's validation is unchanged. A selection that crosses hidden syntax resolves to the raw span that covers it.
3. Reveal: highlight a saved anchor inside the rendered reply, including anchors that start or end inside formatting or code, and anchors saved before this change.
4. Keyboard selection: keep the read-only raw-text selector as the keyboard path, with its offsets unchanged.
5. Streaming: render partial Markdown without flicker or layout jumps; an unfinished code fence displays as code.
6. Map node previews stay plain text; strip syntax for readability without persisting anything.
7. Tests: offset mapping across emphasis, lists, code, tables, math, emoji and repeated phrases; old anchors still reveal. Update scripts/verify-passage-selection.mjs.

title: Generate Mermaid diagrams in an isolated worker and save finished artifacts
description:
## What to build

The server half of Mermaid diagrams. When the tutor decides a diagram would help, it asks for one; a separate worker with its own provider session produces Mermaid source from a minimal frozen task; the server validates the result and saves it as an artifact owned by the originating conversation and message. Only the artifact id, title and a concise description ever enter tutor context.

## Work order

1. Contract: decide and record how the tutor signals a request (for example a fenced directive in its reply that the server removes from the visible reply) and the frozen task handed to the worker: the diagram intent and the minimal relevant excerpt. Never pass the full transcript, the tutor thread id or credentials.
2. Worker: run through the conversation's provider with `thread: null`, as branch compaction does, separate from the tutor session, abortable, and bounded in time and output size. It must work through both server/claude.mjs and server/codex.mjs.
3. Validation: accept only Mermaid source that parses. Reject click, href and script directives, HTML labels and oversized output. Store nothing executable.
4. Storage: add an artifacts table in server/store.mjs (id, conversation, message, kind, status, title, description, source, created) with at least pending, ready and failed. Return a conversation's artifacts with its messages. Check ownership so one tree cannot read or attach another tree's artifact by id.
5. Tutor context: later tutor turns, provider switches and branch compaction see only a short marker with the title and description of a ready artifact; never the worker prompt, the source or the worker transcript.
6. Integration tests with the fixture provider for request, context isolation, validation rejects, ownership and both provider adapters.

title: Add an OpenAI-compatible provider adapter with locally stored endpoint settings
description:
## What to build

The server half of the custom endpoint from IDEA.md: a third provider that talks to any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API, configured with a base URL and API key kept on this machine. It is an explicit learner choice and never a silent fallback for Claude or Codex.

## Work order

1. Design note: record in docs/ the API surface used (chat completions with streaming, model listing), how history is replayed, and where the key is stored. Keep the key in a file in the local app-data directory with owner-only permissions; it is written through the server and never returned to the browser, logged or placed in SQLite.
2. Adapter: server/openai.mjs with the same `models()` and `generate()` shape as server/claude.mjs and server/codex.mjs. The API is stateless, so each turn sends the saved discussion plus the fixed inherited branch context; honour the abort signal; map stream chunks to the existing delta and status events.
3. Settings endpoints: save, test and clear the endpoint with CSRF and the existing loopback checks. Report only whether an endpoint is configured and its base URL.
4. Wiring: register the provider in server/main.mjs only when configured. Branch compaction and provider switching work through it with no special cases.
5. Integration tests against a local fake OpenAI-compatible server: streaming, history replay including inherited context, abort, model catalogue, error mapping, compaction, and that no response body or log contains the key. Extend test/credential-boundary.test.mjs.

## Start here

server/claude.mjs and server/codex.mjs (adapter shape), server/app.mjs (`providers`, `/api/models`), test/provider.test.mjs, test/credential-boundary.test.mjs.

## Out of scope

The settings form and model-menu entry (next task). Provider-specific extras such as tools, vision or the responses API.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- With an endpoint configured, a conversation streams a reply through the adapter, and a follow-up turn shows the earlier discussion and inherited context were sent.
- Stop interrupts the request; endpoint errors surface as an honest message and the conversation stays usable.
- Branch compaction and switching to and from Claude or Codex work through the adapter with the fake server.
- The key is stored only in the owner-only file and appears in no HTTP response, log line or SQLite row; a test scans for it.
- With no endpoint configured, behaviour is unchanged and no API-key path exists for Claude or Codex.
- `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

New provider id openai is registered in main only when configured and dynamically on save/clear; Claude remains default. Settings: GET/POST /api/settings/endpoint, POST /api/settings/endpoint/test, POST /api/settings/endpoint/clear. Existing Host/Origin/cross-site/JSON/CSRF boundaries apply. title: Offer the custom endpoint in settings and the model menu
description:
## What to build

The learner-facing half of the custom endpoint: a settings form to add, test and remove it, and its models in the compact model menu next to Claude and Codex.

## Work order

1. Settings: in the existing Connections area add base URL and API key fields with Save, Test connection and Remove. The key field never shows a saved key back. State plainly that requests go to that endpoint and are billed by its owner.
2. Model menu: a third group listing the endpoint's models. When it is not configured or failing, show an actionable item instead of a dead choice, as the menu already does for a signed-out provider.
3. Switching: change a conversation between the custom endpoint, Claude and Codex in every direction; visible history stays intact and the next reply uses the prior discussion and inherited context. Children inherit their parent's provider and model as today.
4. Keyboard: the whole configure, select and switch path works by keyboard alone.
5. Update README.md and the help text; record evidence under docs/verification. Use the fake server for fixtures; run one live check only if the owner has supplied an endpoint, and say so either way.

## Start here

src/ChatPage.tsx (Connections block, model `DropdownMenu`, `changeModel`), the settings endpoints from the previous task, scripts/verify-model-switch.mjs.

## Out of scope

Multiple custom endpoints, per-conversation keys, usage or cost display.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- An endpoint can be added, tested and removed from settings by mouse and keyboard; a saved key is never displayed.
- Its models appear in the model menu; an unconfigured or failing endpoint shows an actionable message.
- A conversation switches among the custom endpoint, Claude and Codex in each direction, in a root and in a nested child, keeping visible history and continuing with prior context; verified again after restart.
- New trees still default to Claude.
- README and help describe the feature; the evidence note says whether a live endpoint was tested.

Defaults: Test saved configuration only, explicit Save to replace URL/key, do not choose provider on save; settings/menu failures actionable; no extra endpoint/key scopes/cost UI. title: Show video status and a paused native player inline
description:
## What to build

The learner-facing half of requested videos: an artifact entry at the request's position in the chat with honest status, and a paused native player once the file is ready, without interrupting chat.

## Work order

1. Insert the artifact entry at its original position with a descriptive title and the states from the proposal's table that generation can reach today: Preparing, Rendering, Ready and Failed. Show render progress only when the renderer reports it.
2. Ready state: title, concise text explanation and an inline native `<video>` player, initially paused, kept within the chat width with its aspect ratio. No autoplay.
3. Completion must not move keyboard focus, scroll the conversation or inject generation messages. The learner can keep chatting and navigate elsewhere while a job runs; the result appears only in the originating conversation.
4. Accessibility: one labelled status announcement per state change, not per progress tick. Tab reaches the player. The player owns its keys while focused, so map and chat handlers must not intercept them.
5. Map node transcript shows a compact "Video: title" row with its status.
6. Reload restores a ready video from the local file with no provider request.
7. Browser fixture for the status sequence, keyboard playback, no stolen focus or scroll, and reload.

## Start here

docs/video-flow-proposal.md "Learner flow" and its acceptance checks 1 and 6. src/ChatPage.tsx and the Mermaid artifact card.

## Out of scope

Cancel, Retry, Interrupted and Unavailable handling (TreeTutor-vm4.3). Captions unless speech was added.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- Request a video inside a nested child, navigate away and chat elsewhere while it generates: the finished player appears only in its original conversation.
- The player starts paused; play, pause, seek, volume and fullscreen work by keyboard through native controls; focus and scroll position are not taken when the result arrives.
- Status changes are announced once each; progress ticks are not announced.
- The text explanation is present alongside the video.
- Reload shows the ready video with no provider request.
- `npm test`, `npm run build`, the Astryx built-output doctor and the fixture pass.
notes:
2026-11-10 implemented and verified (TreeTutor-vm4.10). Evidence: docs/verification/video-player.md, docs/verification/video-player-results.json.
What: src/VideoCard.tsx inline entry (Preparing/Rendering/Ready/Failed; progress bar only when renderer reports; paused native <video controls>, no autoplay, chat width, 16:9 frame reserved while pending so completion does not shift layout; card aria-live=off with one role=status line per state). Server: in-memory job phase/progress merged into tree GET and previews, /api/state.videos drives client polling after the reply; renderer prints 5% progress; media endpoint serves single byte ranges for seeking. Map row "Video: title · status". Chat Escape ignores focused video.
Decisions/tradeoffs: phase/progress kept in memory, not SQLite (restart already fails pending jobs; vm4.3 owns Interrupted). Failed card shows server reason; Retry is vm4.3.
Evidence: npm test 85/85 PASS (fixture integration + live sandboxed Remotion render, no provider); browser fixture scripts/verify-video-player.mjs 9/9 PASS (synthetic providers, real sandboxed render, prod build, headless Chrome 157): nested-child placement, chatting elsewhere, status sequence with exactly 2 status texts while progress changed, no focus/scroll/message change on completion, keyboard play/pause/seek/volume/fullscreen with no app interception, origin-only result, reload with zero provider calls. npm run build PASS; astryx doctor --built dist 0 fail (2 existing font warnings).
Limits: Chrome only; no native fullscreen/mute keys in Chrome (fullscreen via native button by Tab+Enter); screen-reader speech not observed; no native provider run in this task.

title: Offer grounded branch suggestions after saved replies
description:
## What to build

The first half of automatic suggestions, following docs/branch-suggestions-proposal.md: after a reply completes and is saved, evaluate it once for zero to three grounded passages, show them in a compact "Explore further" group under that reply, and let the learner turn one into a branch through the existing editable branch form. This is the original idea's one-click break-down of a subproblem.

## Work order

1. Trigger: evaluate once per successfully saved completed reply, using the provider and model captured at completion and only the completed answer, its question and the fixed inherited context. Run it as a separate `generate` call with `thread: null` so nothing enters tutor history. Never evaluate partial, failed, cancelled or interrupted replies, and never rerun on focus, reopen or provider change.
2. Validation: each candidate is one contiguous passage with message id, exact text and UTF-16 start and end offsets into the saved reply. Reuse the boundary and exact-slice checks from the branches endpoint in server/app.mjs. Discard mismatches, duplicates, overlaps and ungrounded candidates rather than guess. Cover repeated phrases and emoji.
3. Storage: save completed candidates with their source message, separate from tutor messages.
4. UI: the group appears after its source reply without popups, focus moves or scrolling, with one polite availability announcement. Choosing a suggestion opens the existing branch form with the exact passage and an editable question; only submitting creates and focuses a child through the normal compaction flow; cancelling creates nothing and returns focus to the suggestion. Manual selection keeps working throughout.
5. Failure: show a brief non-blocking "Suggestions unavailable" status; no automatic retry.
6. Integration tests with the fixture provider for trigger rules, validation, isolation and the submit boundary; a browser fixture for keyboard choose, edit, cancel and submit.

## Start here

docs/branch-suggestions-proposal.md (selected design) and its acceptance checks 1, 2, 3 and 5. server/app.mjs (reply completion in the message handler, the branches endpoint), src/ChatPage.tsx (`Passage`, branch form).

## Out of scope

Dismissals, accepted-child reuse, restart and late-event handling, and the learning-example quality review (TreeTutor-vm4.5). Learner profiles, ranking, preferences, automatic child creation.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- Complete replies in two conversations at once: each receives zero to three candidates only after its own saved completion, while typing, navigation and focus stay uninterrupted. Failed, partial and cancelled replies trigger nothing.
- Every displayed candidate's offsets resolve to its exact text in the saved reply; repeated text, emoji, invalid offsets, duplicates and overlaps are handled and invalid candidates never appear.
- Choose, edit, cancel and submit by keyboard alone: cancel creates nothing; submit creates exactly one focused child with the ordinary fixed snapshot.
- Model requests and saved histories show only the stated input reaching suggestion generation; candidates and diagnostics stay out of tutor history, including in a nested child.
- An empty result shows no group; a failure shows the non-blocking status and manual branching still works.

title: Generate a requested video in a bounded isolated worker
description:
## What to build

The generation half of requested videos, following docs/video-flow-proposal.md: an explicit learner request creates a job; an isolated worker writes a Remotion composition and renders a finished local file; the server validates and publishes it as an artifact. No player UI yet beyond what tests need.

## Work order

1. Request: detect an explicit video request in the conversation and save a job with the frozen input from the proposal's contract (exact request, relevant saved excerpt, fixed inherited context, source ids). An ordinary explanation never starts a video. When intent is unclear the tutor asks first.
2. Worker: a dedicated workspace per attempt under the local app-data directory, outside the repository, with no tutor credentials, no access to unrelated learning files, bounded run time and controlled network access. Record the actual sandbox and provider permission settings used; context isolation and execution isolation are checked separately.
3. Render: add Remotion and render programmatically to a private temporary output. Validate that the output path stays inside the workspace, the media is readable and the job owns it, then move it to its final location before marking the artifact ready. A failed save never shows a playable success.
4. Storage and serving: reuse the Mermaid artifacts table for job, attempt, status and result description. Serve finished media only through a same-origin artifact endpoint with ownership checks; never accept a generated absolute path or URL as a media source.
5. Tutor context: only artifact id, title and the concise finished-content description. No source code, logs, transcript or filesystem paths.
6. Integration tests for the job lifecycle to ready, path and ownership validation, and context isolation. One real render, kept short, as recorded evidence.

## Start here

docs/video-flow-proposal.md (selected design), PRD.md "Isolated media generation", and the artifact pipeline delivered for Mermaid.

## Out of scope

The inline player and status UI (next task). Retry, cancel and restart recovery (TreeTutor-vm4.3). Narration, captions, editing, gallery.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- An explicit request in a conversation creates exactly one job with the frozen input; an ordinary explanation creates none.
- The worker runs in its own workspace without tutor credentials or unrelated learning files; the evidence note records the real permission and network settings and how each was checked.
- A finished render is validated and published as a ready artifact served only through the same-origin endpoint; an out-of-workspace path, unreadable media or a failed save publishes nothing.
- Tutor history, provider-switch history and branch snapshots contain only id, title and description.
- One real short render completes and its evidence is recorded. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
notes:
Implemented 2026-11-09 (TreeTutor-vm4.9).

What: tutor requests a video via a hidden fenced `treetutor-video` block (same JSON shape as diagrams); the server starts a job only when the learner's own message names a video/animation/clip/movie (asksForVideo), so an ordinary explanation never starts one even if the model emits the block. Tutor instructions tell it to ask first when intent is unclear. Job = artifacts row (kind 'video', attempt, frozen `input` JSON: request, intent, excerpt, inheritedContext {snapshot, selectedPassage, question}, sources {conversation, requestMessage, replyMessage, parentConversation, parentMessage}). The job runs detached from the reply stream (learner can keep chatting); app.stop aborts it. Files: server/videos.mjs, server/video-render.mjs, store migration (CHECK kind IN mermaid/video; old Mermaid DBs rebuilt in place, verified with a HEAD-schema DB), app media endpoint GET /api/trees/:tree/artifacts/:id/media.

Isolation settings actually used:
- Composing agent (context isolation): existing provider adapters with a fresh session (thread null), separate WORKER instructions, input = frozen JSON only. Claude: `-p --max-turns 1 --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {} --setting-sources '' --disable-slash-commands`, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/AUTH_TOKEN stripped, cwd <appdata>/claude-workspace. Codex: shell/apply_patch/js_repl/code_mode/apps/skills off, web_search disabled, every tool request rejected. The agent has no file, shell or network tools; it returns source text, which the server validates (imports only react/remotion, no dynamic import/require/fetch/network APIs/URLs/media elements, ≤64 KiB, required `// Description:` line) and writes into the attempt workspace.
- Render (execution isolation): `bwrap --ro-bind / / --tmpfs $HOME --tmpfs <appdata> --tmpfs /tmp --tmpfs /run/user --ro-bind <repo>/node_modules --ro-bind server/video-render.mjs --bind <workspace> --unshare-all --die-with-parent --new-session --clearenv` (env HOME/PATH/TMPDIR only + PWD), SIGKILL after 180 s; composition step bounded at 120 s. Chromium = pre-installed node_modules/.remotion chrome-headless-shell (no download in sandbox). Checked by test "render sandbox hides home and app data…": app-data DB, ~/.claude and repo files denied, writes outside workspace denied, TCP to 1.1.1.1:443 denied, env = HOME,PATH,PWD,TMPDIR.
- Workspace: <appdata>/video-work/<attempt> (outside repo; default ~/.local/share/treetutor). After each attempt bundle/tmp/out are removed (41 MB bundle); Video.tsx/index.tsx kept as private work.
- Publish: server-chosen out/<uuid>.mp4; realpath must equal <realpath workspace>/out/<name>, regular non-symlink file, 1 KiB–200 MiB, `ftyp` header, duration 0–60 s, row still pending with same attempt → rename to <appdata>/videos/<artifact id>.mp4 → finishVideo; DB failure unlinks the file. Media path is derived from artifact id only; endpoint requires conversation ownership + kind video + ready. fs errors are replaced with generic messages (no paths).
- Tutor context: ready videos appear as `Ready artifacts (artifact metadata): [{id, kind, title, description}]` in tutor/provider-switch history and compaction prompts.

Evidence:
- Fixture (npm test, test/videos.test.mjs): lifecycle to ready with frozen input in nested child, ordinary explanation creates none, worker gets only frozen input, same-origin media + wrong-conversation 404, tutor/switch/branch histories hold only id/title/description (no source marker, paths, attempt or input); symlinked output, replaced out dir, missing/unreadable media, render failure, lost ownership and failed save publish nothing; failed job is marked failed and media 404s.
- Live (sandboxed render, no provider): real Remotion render in bwrap, 1 s composition, ~8.4 s, in npm test (skips only if bwrap/browser missing).
- Live end-to-end with Claude (sonnet, subscription CLI): composition written by Claude, rendered in sandbox, published ready: 8 s, 67 KB MP4, 30.7 s total; description "A tournament tree with four players: two semifinal matches each produce a winner, and the two winners slide up along the branches into the final node, where the champion is highlighted." Frame at 6 s inspected: tree with Ana/Dan advancing (some label overlap — generated quality, not validated). Codex not exercised live for video.
- npm test 84/84 pass; npm run build pass; astryx doctor --built dist: fail 0.

Decisions/tradeoffs: invalid or non-completed video requests create no job (no failed card) — simplest; status UI is next task. Media served whole-file without Range (shortcut comment; add with player). Status set stays pending/ready/failed (no preparing/rendering split yet). Restart marks pending videos failed with a video-specific message; full interrupted/retry semantics remain TreeTutor-vm4.3. Remotion 4.0.542 (remotion, @remotion/renderer, @remotion/bundler) added; browser fetched once via ensureBrowser into node_modules/.remotion (needs `npx remotion browser ensure`-style step on fresh installs — currently manual).

Cancel affects only that job; late events from canceled or superseded attempts cannot publish ready.
Restart marks unfinished work interrupted without automatic inference; ready media persists and missing files show unavailable with explicit regeneration.
Simulate rendering, persistence and invalid-output failures; status stays honest, other chats work, and generation work stays outside model history.

### TreeTutor-vm4.3: Generate isolated Remotion videos on learner request
Learner requests video and plays finished artifact inline; generation working messages, code, tool output and revisions stay outside tutor context; task/result follows agreed design; failure leaves chat usable.
